answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must accumulate a yarrow-scored history of verified micro-responses to unpredictable prompts over weeks; only accounts reaching a threshold zenith unlock the shared vault of agent services. Enforcement: history is non-transferable and cryptographically bound to one runtime. Attacker cost: sustaining many identities means paying continuous human-like attention time per account, which scales linearly and cannot be parallelized cheaply.
